translation:
Dudhrej

_Jivandas uchit abhidhana, sant mahant dhimant samana |_
_Suni Shatpragnaswami yash kirtan, Dudhrej aaye sumudit man ||_
(Jivandas, fitly so named, the equal of the saints, the mahants and the wise; having heard the kirtan (hymn) sung in praise of Shatpragnaswami, he came to Dudhrej with a gladdened mind.)

It is stated therein that Jivanji Maharaj came to Dudhrej together with about five hundred renunciant sants (ascetic saints). At that time a miracle is also mentioned as having occurred there. To prepare food for all the sants and devotees they searched for milk, but not enough was found; so, on Chhathabava's instruction, they filled and brought water from the lake there, Dugdhsar, and in those cauldrons it turned into milk. From it dudhpak (a milk pudding) was made.

Kantikumar Bhatt has given information about this on pages 23-27 of the book on Jivanji and Jivanji's devotees. Thus this Dudhrej is filled with the memory of Jivanji, and therefore it is a punya sthali (a sacred, blessed place).
